answer: A hollow shell of fake identities collapses when each one must custody a unique encrypted shard. Every agent stores a distinct slice of the network archive and answers random byte-range challenges; a missed proof forfeits its bond, so N fakes need N disks' worth of live storage, not one copied file. A walnut-sized shard per identity keeps honest costs low, and the horizon for attackers is linear: ten thousand fakes mean ten thousand drives. Limit: storage is cheap in bulk, so shard size and challenge frequency must track disk prices.
